explanation: Century years are leap years only if they divide exactly by 400. That rule makes the average year 365.2425 days, within about half a minute of the solar year.

claims.text: In the Gregorian calendar, 2000 was a leap year.
In the Gregorian calendar, 1700, 1800 and 1900 were not leap years.
In the Gregorian calendar, a century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by 400.
The average Gregorian calendar year is 365.2425 days long, since 97 of every 400 years are leap years.
The mean solar (tropical) year is about 365.2422 days, so the Gregorian average differs from it by about half a minute.
